name: lighthouse-perf-budget
outcome: FAIL_BUDGET — performance below 0.70 on 7 of 10 URLs (warn-level)
approach: Lighthouse mobile 4G profile (375×812, 1.6Mbps, 4× CPU slowdown) on 10 routes via @lhci/cli. Categories: a11y/best-practices/seo passing, performance under threshold.

top_opportunities_aggregate.explanation: One URL has massive offscreen-image deferral opportunity. Likely the destination detail page hero/below-fold gallery.
5 URLs serve images larger than rendered size. <Image sizes="..."> attribute is too generous, picking 1600w variant when 800w would suffice.
5 URLs serve some assets as JPG instead of WebP. Most destination images use WebP via image-loader.ts but some root-level pngs (icon-192, og-image) and .jpg fallbacks are still raster.
Polyfills/transpiled code being shipped to modern browsers. Likely browserslist target too conservative or a third-party script.
Few resources still on HTTP/1.1 — investigate which CDN endpoint.
Small but ubiquitous — likely unused parts of vendor bundles.

carried_forward.title: Image size opportunity sweep
carried_forward.description: Audit `sizes` props on every <Image> component. Cards in explore-grid render at ~33vw on desktop, ~50vw on tablet, 100vw on mobile — but `sizes="(max-width: 640px) 100vw, (max-width: 1024px) 50vw, 33vw"` may still pull 1600w on retina mobile. Tighten to actual rendered widths.

carried_forward.title: Browserslist tightening
carried_forward.description: Check apps/web/package.json `browserslist` and remove ES5 targets. Modern Vercel deploys can target ES2020+ for ~70KB savings.

carried_forward.title: Investigate offscreen-images on the 1.8M-savings URL
carried_forward.description: The single-hit savings of 1.8s suggests one route has ~10 hero images all set to priority=true or eager-loaded.
carried_forward.next_step: Run `lighthouse --view <url>` locally on each URL, sort opportunities by savings, find the largest
